title: Stores and Warehouses
readerIntent: Model sales channels and flexible fulfillment locations.
priorKnowledge: Understand enterprise, country, channel, and Storefront context.
owner: Store owns selling-location/channel configuration; Inventory owns warehouses and sourcing eligibility
summary: Stores represent commercial customer touchpoints; warehouses represent stock-holding or fulfillment locations that can serve configurable scopes.

sections.heading: Store model
items: A Store may represent physical retail, digital commerce, marketplace, service, or another configured sales context.
It relates to enterprise, countries, channels, websites, catalogs, currencies, languages, warehouses, and operational policy without taking ownership of those models.
A physical Store can also be a fulfillment or pickup location when Inventory configuration permits it.

sections.heading: Warehouse flexibility
items: Enterprise creates warehouses for countries, zones, areas, stores, delivery purposes, or customer segments.
One warehouse may serve several scopes; a scope may source from prioritized warehouses.
Sellability and service-area rules are separate from physical balance.
A product can be available in three delivery zones and intentionally unavailable or unsellable in two others.

sections.heading: Governance
items: Relationships preserve tenant and enterprise boundaries.
Activation, service scope, priority, capacity, pickup, delivery, exclusion, and fallback are configurable.
Source selection remains Inventory-owned; Storefront and Store do not calculate stock.
